# Demographic Profile for Alberta-like Synthetic Case Notes

## Overview
This demographic profile establishes realistic parameters for generating fictional case notes consistent with Alberta social services populations. All data is synthetic and for modeling purposes only.

---

## 1. Age Distribution Patterns

### Primary Working-Age Population (18-64)
- **18-35 years**: 28%
  - Early career/entry-level employment
  - Higher housing instability rates
  - Vulnerable to income disruptions
  
- **36-50 years**: 35%
  - Mid-career employment
  - Higher family responsibilities
  - More stable housing but vulnerable to job loss
  
- **51-64 years**: 22%
  - Pre-retirement employment
  - Chronic health conditions emerging
  - Limited retraining opportunities

### Secondary Senior Population (65-80)
- **65-72 years**: 10%
  - Early pension recipients
  - Mixed independent/dependent living
  
- **73-80 years**: 5%
  - Increased care support needs
  - Fixed income constraints

---

## 2. Gender Distribution & Family Structures

### Gender Split
- **Female**: 54%
- **Male**: 44%
- **Non-binary/Other**: 2%

### Family Structure Breakdown
| Structure | Percentage | Notes |
|-----------|-----------|-------|
| Single, no dependents | 32% | Primary vulnerable group |
| Single parent (1 child) | 18% | Mostly female-headed |
| Single parent (2+ children) | 12% | High support needs |
| Couple, no dependents | 16% | Diverse age ranges |
| Couple with children | 18% | Mixed employment patterns |
| Multi-generational household | 4% | Often immigrant/refugee |

### Household Composition Notes
- Average household size: 2.3 persons
- Single-parent households: 30% (higher than provincial average)
- Grandparent-led households: ~3% of cases

---

## 3. Geographic Spread (Alberta-like)

### Urban/Rural Distribution
- **Major City Centers** (Calgary/Edmonton equivalents): 58%
  - High service density
  - More employment opportunities
  - Higher housing costs
  - Better transit access
  
- **Secondary Cities**: 22%
  - Moderate service availability
  - Limited employment diversity
  - More affordable housing
  - Car-dependent
  
- **Rural/Small Communities**: 20%
  - Sparse services
  - Transportation barriers
  - Community-reliant support
  - Agriculture/resource-based economy

### Regional Economic Drivers (Fictional)
- Energy sector fluctuations (primary economic influence)
- Agriculture/ranching (rural areas)
- Small business/service sector (secondary cities)
- Government employment (stable across regions)

---

## 4. Employment Status Distribution

### Primary Employment Categories
| Status | Percentage | Key Characteristics |
|--------|-----------|-------------------|
| Employed Full-time | 42% | 35-40 hrs/week, stable income |
| Employed Part-time | 18% | 15-30 hrs/week, variable income |
| Gig/Contract/Casual | 12% | Irregular income, no benefits |
| Unemployed (seeking) | 14% | Active job search, recent job loss |
| Not in labor force | 8% | Disability, caregiving, school |
| Retired/Pension | 6% | Seniors on fixed income |

### Income Levels (Monthly Gross)
- **Below $2,000**: 24% (vulnerable group)
- **$2,000-$3,500**: 28% (lower-middle income)
- **$3,500-$5,000**: 26% (middle income)
- **Above $5,000**: 22% (stable income)

### Employment Barriers Noted
- Limited education (30% without high school completion)
- Disability/health limitations (25%)
- Childcare responsibilities (18%)
- Transportation barriers (15%)
- Recent arrival/language barriers (12%)

---

## 5. Housing Stability Patterns

### Housing Status Distribution
| Status | Percentage | Characteristics |
|--------|-----------|-----------------|
| Own home/mortgage | 18% | Stable, financial commitment |
| Rent (secure lease) | 48% | 12+ month lease, stable |
| Rent (month-to-month) | 18% | Unstable, eviction risk |
| Temporary/Transitional | 8% | Shelter, emergency housing |
| Precarious | 5% | Doubled-up, couch-surfing |
| Unhoused | 3% | Street, vehicle, outdoor |

### Housing Cost Burden
- **<30% of income**: 32% (affordable)
- **30-50% of income**: 38% (cost-burdened)
- **>50% of income**: 25% (severe burden)
- **N/A (no fixed housing)**: 5%

### Housing Quality Issues
- Substandard conditions: 12%
- Overcrowding (>1 person/room): 8%
- No private sleeping space: 3%
- Utilities unstable/cutoff risk: 9%

### Geographic Housing Patterns
- **Urban centers**: Higher rent costs, more accessible services
- **Secondary cities**: Moderate costs, limited rental supply
- **Rural areas**: Lower costs, longer wait for services

---

## 6. Demographic Risk Intersections

### High-Risk Profile Cluster
- **Age**: 25-35
- **Family**: Single parent (1-2 children)
- **Geography**: Urban center
- **Employment**: Part-time/gig work
- **Housing**: Month-to-month rental, >40% income burden
- **Prevalence**: ~8% of population

### Vulnerable Senior Cluster
- **Age**: 70+
- **Family**: Single/widowed
- **Geography**: Any (service proximity important)
- **Employment**: Fixed pension income
- **Housing**: Rented apartment/subsidized
- **Prevalence**: ~4% of population

### Stability Cluster (Lower Risk)
- **Age**: 40-55
- **Family**: Couple or established single
- **Geography**: Secondary city
- **Employment**: Full-time stable employment
- **Housing**: Own or secure long-term lease
- **Prevalence**: ~28% of population

---

## 7. Demographic Diversity Considerations

### Immigrant/Refugee Populations: 11%
- Language barriers (5% primary language not English)
- Credential recognition barriers
- Shorter tenure (affects eligibility)
- Extended family obligations

### Indigenous Peoples: 7%
- Overrepresented in vulnerable populations
- Historical trauma factors
- Community connection importance
- Health disparities

### LGBTQ2S+ Populations: 4%
- Higher homelessness risk
- Family estrangement
- Employment discrimination
- Mental health factors

### Disability Status: 22%
- Physical disability: 9%
- Cognitive/learning disability: 8%
- Mental health disability: 11%
- (Multiple disabilities possible)

---

## 8. Synthetic Population Summary

**Total Synthetic Caseload Base**: 5,000 fictional individuals

### Age Breakdown (n=5,000)
- 18-35: 1,400
- 36-50: 1,750
- 51-64: 1,100
- 65-72: 500
- 73-80: 250

### Geographic Breakdown (n=5,000)
- Major cities: 2,900
- Secondary cities: 1,100
- Rural areas: 1,000

### Housing Stability Breakdown (n=5,000)
- Stable housing: 3,200
- Precarious housing: 1,300
- Unhoused: 500

---

## 9. Case Note Generation Parameters

Use these distributions when creating synthetic case notes:

1. **Randomize within distributions** above
2. **Create realistic intersections** (e.g., don't pair high income with housing instability uniformly)
3. **Maintain geographic consistency** (rural cases show transportation barriers)
4. **Age-appropriate employment** (seniors have pensions, not gig work)
5. **Family structure authenticity** (housing impacts vary by family type)
6. **Seasonal employment patterns** (energy sector, agriculture show variation)

---

## 10. Notes on Realism & Ethical Considerations

- ✓ These distributions reflect real Alberta-like populations
- ✓ Vulnerable populations intentionally included for realistic modeling
- ✓ All individuals are completely fictional
- ✓ Use for training, research, and system design only
- ✗ Do not use to make assumptions about real individuals
- ✗ Do not target real populations based on these profiles
- ✗ Do not use to reduce funding or services

---

**Status**: Complete - Ready for Case Note Generation Phase
**Version**: 1.0

## Objective
Create a comprehensive synthetic case note generator using a three mode noise injection methodology. This approach systematically introduces different types of realistic variation into synthetic case notes through controlled noise injection.

## Three-Lane Noise Injection Methodology
This approach introduces controlled variation through three specialized generation lanes, each targeting different aspects of realistic case note variation:

### Lane 1: Professional Baseline Noise (60% = 300 cases)
- **Purpose**: Establish consistent professional documentation standards as baseline
- **Noise Type**: Minimal variation, standardized professional language patterns
- **Target**: Clean baseline cases for algorithm calibration and control groups
- **Documentation Style**: Single standard professional caseworker voice

### Lane 2: Writer Style Noise (25% = 125 cases)
- **Purpose**: Inject realistic human inconsistencies in documentation practices
- **Noise Type**: Experience-based writing variation, quality fluctuations, stylistic differences
- **Target**: Test algorithm robustness against real-world documentation variability
- **Documentation Styles**: New caseworker (30%), experienced (50%), senior (20%) with quality variation

### Lane 3: Scenario Embedding Noise (15% = 75 cases)
- **Purpose**: Embed specific algorithmic testing scenarios and patterns
- **Noise Type**: Targeted terminology, crisis patterns, service connection indicators
- **Target**: Validate specific algorithm detection capabilities
- **Documentation Focus**: Housing crises, mental health deterioration, successful service connections

## Technical Requirements

### Core Architecture
- **Total Cases**: 500 synthetic cases (matching existing output)
- **ID Range**: SYN_00001 to SYN_00500 (sequential, no gaps)
- **Random Seed**: Configurable base seed with consistent lane coordination
- **Output Schema**: Identical to existing: `person_oid,first_name,last_name,gender,age,complexity_level,archetype_id, writer_style,embedded_scenarios,case_note`

Create clearly documented parameter sections and implement comprehensive validation to ensure each lane achieves its intended noise injection targets. The goal is to provide a robust, reproducible methodology for controlled noise injection in synthetic case note generation, optimized for algorithm validation and testing workflows.

#' Generate formatted case ID

generate_case_id <- function(index) {
  sprintf("%s_%s", 
          CONFIG$id_prefix, 
          str_pad(index, width = CONFIG$id_padding, pad = "0"))
}

#' Replace template placeholders
#' @param template Template string with [PLACEHOLDER] syntax
#' @param replacements Named list of placeholder values
#' @return Text with placeholders replaced
fill_template <- function(template, replacements) {
  result <- template
  for (placeholder in names(replacements)) {
    result <- str_replace_all(
      result, 
      sprintf("\\[%s\\]", placeholder), 
      replacements[[placeholder]]
    )
  }
  result
}

#' Introduce realistic writing errors (Lane 2)
#' @param text Input text
#' @param error_types Vector of error types to apply
#' @param error_probability Probability of introducing errors
#' @return Text with introduced errors
introduce_writing_errors <- function(text, error_types = c(), error_probability = 0.15) {
  if (length(error_types) == 0 || runif(1) > error_probability) {
    return(text)
  }
  
  error_type <- sample(error_types, 1)
  
  switch(error_type,
    typo = {
      # Introduce random character substitution
      words <- str_split(text, " ")[[1]]
      if (length(words) > 2) {
        word_idx <- sample(1:length(words), 1)
        word <- words[word_idx]
        if (nchar(word) > 3) {
          char_idx <- sample(1:nchar(word), 1)
          typo_word <- str_sub(word, char_idx, char_idx)
          substr(words[word_idx], char_idx, char_idx) <- 
            sample(letters, 1)
          text <- paste(words, collapse = " ")
        }
      }
      text
    },
    passive_voice = {
      # Convert to more passive constructions
      text <- str_replace_all(text, "client ", "the client ")
      text <- str_replace_all(text, "we ", "it was ")
      text
    },
    redundancy = {
      # Add redundant phrases
      if (runif(1) > 0.5) {
        text <- str_c(text, " ", str_sub(text, 1, 50), "...")
      }
      text
    },
    vagueness = {
      # Replace specific terms with vague ones
      text <- str_replace_all(text, "depression", "mental health issues")
      text <- str_replace_all(text, "housing", "living situation")
      text
    },
    text
  )
}

#' Apply abbreviations (Lane 2)
#' @param text Input text
#' @param abbreviations Named character vector of abbreviations
#' @param probability Probability of applying abbreviations
#' @return Text with abbreviations applied
apply_abbreviations <- function(text, abbreviations = c(), probability = 0.2) {
  if (length(abbreviations) == 0 || runif(1) > probability) {
    return(text)
  }
  
  for (full_form in names(abbreviations)) {
    if (runif(1) > 0.5) {
      text <- str_replace_all(text, fixed(full_form), abbreviations[full_form])
    }
  }
  text
}

#' Generate random date within range
#' @param n Number of dates
#' @return Vector of dates
generate_random_dates <- function(n = 1) {
  dates <- sample(
    seq(CONFIG$start_date, CONFIG$end_date, by = "day"),
    size = n,
    replace = TRUE
  )
  format(dates, "%m/%d/%Y")
}

#' Generate follow-up date (typically 1-4 weeks later)
#' @param reference_date Base date in character format
#' @return Follow-up date string
generate_followup_date <- function(reference_date) {
  ref <- as.Date(reference_date, "%m/%d/%Y")
  days_ahead <- sample(7:28, 1)  # 1-4 weeks
  followup <- ref + days_ahead
  if (followup > CONFIG$end_date) {
    followup <- CONFIG$end_date
  }
  format(followup, "%m/%d/%Y")
}

validate_case_notes <- function(df) {
  
  cat("\n=== VALIDATION REPORT ===\n\n")
  
  validation_results <- list(
    passed = TRUE,
    issues = character()
  )
  
  # Check required columns
  missing_cols <- setdiff(CONFIG$validation$required_fields, colnames(df))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    validation_results$passed <- FALSE
    validation_results$issues <- c(
      validation_results$issues,
      sprintf("Missing columns: %s", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
    )
  } else {
    cat("✓ All required columns present\n")
  }
  
  # Check row count
  if (nrow(df) != CONFIG$total_cases) {
    validation_results$passed <- FALSE
    validation_results$issues <- c(
      validation_results$issues,
      sprintf("Expected %d rows, got %d", CONFIG$total_cases, nrow(df))
    )
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("✓ Correct number of rows: %d\n", nrow(df)))
  }
  
  # Check ID format and uniqueness
  id_pattern <- sprintf("^%s_\\d{%d}$", CONFIG$id_prefix, CONFIG$id_padding)
  valid_ids <- grepl(id_pattern, df$person_oid)
  if (!all(valid_ids)) {
    validation_results$passed <- FALSE
    validation_results$issues <- c(
      validation_results$issues,
      sprintf("Invalid ID format in %d rows", sum(!valid_ids))
    )
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("✓ All IDs have valid format\n")  )
  }
  
  if (length(unique(df$person_oid)) != nrow(df)) {
    validation_results$passed <- FALSE
    validation_results$issues <- c(
      validation_results$issues,
      "Duplicate person_oid values detected"
    )
  } else {
    cat("✓ All person_oid values are unique\n")
  }
  
  # Check case note length
  note_lengths <- nchar(df$case_note)
  invalid_lengths <- note_lengths < CONFIG$validation$min_note_length | 
                     note_lengths > CONFIG$validation$max_note_length
  if (any(invalid_lengths)) {
    validation_results$passed <- FALSE
    validation_results$issues <- c(
      validation_results$issues,
      sprintf("%d case notes outside length bounds [%d-%d]", 
              sum(invalid_lengths),
              CONFIG$validation$min_note_length,
              CONFIG$validation$max_note_length)
    )
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("✓ All case notes within length bounds [%d-%d]\n",
                CONFIG$validation$min_note_length,
                CONFIG$validation$max_note_length))
  }
  
  # Lane distribution analysis
  lane1_count <- sum(df$embedded_scenarios == "None")
  lane2_count <- sum(df$embedded_scenarios == "Writing Style Variation")
  lane3_count <- nrow(df) - lane1_count - lane2_count
  
  cat(sprintf("\n✓ Lane Distribution Analysis:\n"))
  cat(sprintf("  Lane 1 (Professional Baseline): %d (%.1f%%)\n", 
              lane1_count, 100 * lane1_count / nrow(df)))
  cat(sprintf("  Lane 2 (Writer Style Noise): %d (%.1f%%)\n", 
              lane2_count, 100 * lane2_count / nrow(df)))
  cat(sprintf("  Lane 3 (Scenario Embedding): %d (%.1f%%)\n", 
              lane3_count, 100 * lane3_count / nrow(df)))
  
  # Writer style distribution (Lane 2 specific)
  writer_styles <- df %>%
    filter(embedded_scenarios == "Writing Style Variation") %>%
    group_by(writer_style) %>%
    summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
    arrange(desc(count))
  
  if (nrow(writer_styles) > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("\n✓ Writer Style Distribution (Lane 2):\n"))
    for (i in 1:nrow(writer_styles)) {
      pct <- 100 * writer_styles$count[i] / lane2_count
      cat(sprintf("  %s: %d (%.1f%%)\n", 
                  writer_styles$writer_style[i], 
                  writer_styles$count[i], 
                  pct))
    }
  }
  
  # Embedded scenarios distribution (Lane 3 specific)
  scenarios <- df %>%
    filter(embedded_scenarios != "None" & 
           embedded_scenarios != "Writing Style Variation") %>%
    group_by(embedded_scenarios) %>%
    summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
    arrange(desc(count))
  
  if (nrow(scenarios) > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("\n✓ Embedded Scenarios Distribution (Lane 3):\n"))
    for (i in 1:nrow(scenarios)) {
      pct <- 100 * scenarios$count[i] / lane3_count
      cat(sprintf("  %s: %d (%.1f%%)\n", 
                  scenarios$embedded_scenarios[i], 
                  scenarios$count[i], 
                  pct))
    }
  }
  
  # Complexity distribution
  complexity_dist <- table(df$complexity_level)
  cat(sprintf("\n✓ Complexity Level Distribution:\n"))
  for (level in names(complexity_dist)) {
    pct <- 100 * complexity_dist[level] / nrow(df)
    cat(sprintf("  %s: %d (%.1f%%)\n", level, complexity_dist[level], pct))
  }
  
  # Print issues if any
  if (!validation_results$passed) {
    cat(sprintf("\n✗ VALIDATION ISSUES:\n"))
    for (issue in validation_results$issues) {
      cat(sprintf("  - %s\n", issue))
    }
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("\n✓ ALL VALIDATION CHECKS PASSED\n"))
  }
  
  invisible(validation_results)
}

analyze_case_note_samples <- function(df, samples_per_lane = 3) {
  
  cat("\n=== SAMPLE CASE NOTES BY LANE ===\n\n")
  
  # Lane 1 samples
  cat("--- LANE 1: PROFESSIONAL BASELINE ---\n\n")
  lane1_samples <- df %>%
    filter(embedded_scenarios == "None") %>%
    sample_n(min(samples_per_lane, sum(embedded_scenarios == "None")))
  
  for (i in 1:nrow(lane1_samples)) {
    row <- lane1_samples[i, ]
    cat(sprintf("Sample 1.%d | ID: %s | Complexity: %s | Writer: %s\n",
                i, row$person_oid, row$complexity_level, row$writer_style))
    cat(sprintf("Note: %s\n\n", 
                str_sub(row$case_note, 1, 200)))
  }
  
  # Lane 2 samples
  cat("\n--- LANE 2: WRITER STYLE NOISE ---\n\n")
  lane2_samples <- df %>%
    filter(embedded_scenarios == "Writing Style Variation") %>%
    sample_n(min(samples_per_lane, 
                 sum(embedded_scenarios == "Writing Style Variation")))
  
  for (i in 1:nrow(lane2_samples)) {
    row <- lane2_samples[i, ]
    cat(sprintf("Sample 2.%d | ID: %s | Complexity: %s | Writer: %s\n",
                i, row$person_oid, row$complexity_level, row$writer_style))
    cat(sprintf("Note: %s\n\n", 
                str_sub(row$case_note, 1, 200)))
  }
  
  # Lane 3 samples
  cat("\n--- LANE 3: SCENARIO EMBEDDING ---\n\n")
  lane3_samples <- df %>%
    filter(!embedded_scenarios %in% c("None", "Writing Style Variation")) %>%
    sample_n(min(samples_per_lane, 
                 sum(!embedded_scenarios %in% c("None", "Writing Style Variation"))))
  
  for (i in 1:nrow(lane3_samples)) {
    row <- lane3_samples[i, ]
    cat(sprintf("Sample 3.%d | ID: %s | Scenario: %s | Complexity: %s\n",
                i, row$person_oid, row$embedded_scenarios, 
                row$complexity_level))
    cat(sprintf("Note: %s\n\n", 
                str_sub(row$case_note, 1, 200)))
  }
}
